findings.criterion: all six — the master plan is the lockable artifact; a corrupted plan cannot verify any criterion
findings.section: whole document (Phase 3 launch-surface item 2; changelog item 1; phase overview)
findings.message: The re-emission claims the corruption is fixed; it is not — it has gotten worse. Concretely: (a) Phase 3's launch-surface item 2 still reads "envelope-measured today (real `" followed by an ENTIRE embedded copy of the round-2 draft — which itself contains, at its own item 2, a second-level embedding of the round-3 document, i.e. the corruption is now RECURSIVE. (b) The North Star appears at least three times (outer copy, embedded-draft copy, embedded-round-3 copy), directly contradicting "Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." (c) The embedded copies retain the double numbering ("Phase 1 — Phase 0", "Phase 2 — Phase 1"…) the changelog claims was collapsed. (d) The changelog's own item 1 is truncated by the same bug mid-sentence ("restored intact (`job_runner`: real envelope `" → another full document). (e) Raw patch syntax (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) sits verbatim in the phase-overview section — the reviser emitted unapplied search/replace blocks into the artifact instead of applying them. Diagnose the mechanism, not just the symptom: every corruption site is the literal `$` character inside backticks ("real envelope `$`") — some substitution step is expanding `$`-in-backticks into the whole document. Until the reviser re-emits from scratch (not by patching the corrupted text) and the `$` glyph survives, this plan cannot lock.

findings.criterion: criteria 2, 4, 5, 6 — pricing, surfaces, backfill, and ship phases exist only inside a corrupted embedding
findings.message: Trace the outer document's own heading sequence: Phase overview → Phase 0 → Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Phase 3 → [embedded foreign document opens mid-item-2] → …the outer document then resumes only at the fragment "distinct per Stage-0 decision 3, plus the pin)" and the changelog. The standalone top-level "Phase 4 — Pricing engine", "Phase 5 — Surfaces", "Phase 6 — Historical backfill", and "Phase 7 — Ship" sections appear ONLY inside the embedded round-2 copy (where Phase 4 appears twice under two different titles: "Phase 4 — Phase 3 — Forward swarm…" and "Phase 4 — Pricing engine…"). A builder (Foreman) parsing top-level headings of the authoritative document gets a plan that ends at Phase 3. Criteria 5 (dollars), 2 (surfaces), 6 (counting), and 4 (backfill) have no authoritative phase text at the document's top level. This is not a formatting nit — it is the difference between an 8-phase plan and a 4-phase plan depending on which nesting level you believe.

findings.criterion: all — an inaccurate self-report on the lock artifact defeats the convergence loop itself
findings.message: The changelog asserts, in past tense and as fact: "The full second copy … is excised; the double phase numbering … is collapsed; … launch-table item 2 is restored intact … Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." Every one of those statements is false of the emitted artifact (see Findings 1–2). For a plan whose entire theme is honest, verifiable claims ("never a fabricated 0", "vacuous-GREEN is a real failure mode here"), the plan document itself shipping a vacuous-GREEN changelog is disqualifying. The reviser's changelog to the Sharks was also 18 lines of "Applied a search/replace patch" with zero content — the review loop cannot converge when the revision record carries no information and the summary claims are unverified. Requirement: the next revision must be a from-scratch re-emission, and its changelog must be checkable against the artifact (e.g., "grep count of '# NORTH STAR' == 1").

findings.criterion: Statement ("Every Anchor surface that shows spend (project rollups, effort metrics, session details)") + criterion 6
findings.section: Phase 2 deferrals vs Phase 3 walk-through vs North Star Statement
findings.message: The Statement names three surfaces: project rollups, EFFORT METRICS, session details. Phase 2 explicitly defers "Per-effort fleet-attribution ROLLUP/QUERY itself — schema-ready now, query surface deferred to a future effort." Yet Phase 3's unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through promises the opposite: "rollups sum child rows into the effort/fleet totals with the backfill provenance visible." Which is it? Either child rows ARE summed into an effort total (then the per-effort query exists this effort and Phase 2's deferral is wrong), or the query is deferred (then Phase 3's promise is unbacked and swarm spend is NOT visible at the effort level — the exact surface a frustrated user looks at after a fleet run: "what did that effort cost me?"). As written, the user's most natural question has no named owner: Phase 5 delivers per-lane + general PROJECT lines only. The existing `effort_view.effort_rollup` surface (which shows per-effort Σtok·time·$ today) is also an enumerated rollup consumer that criterion 6's honest counting must touch — the plan greps for consumers in Phase 5 but never states whether effort tiles gain the measured/child-row numbers or keep showing zeros for swarm-heavy efforts. Resolve the contradiction explicitly and name which phase makes effort metrics true.

findings.criterion: criteria 2 and 3 — surfaces must render honestly-provenanced states, and the deferral machinery is user-visible
findings.message: The frustrated-UX walk: a user closes a session while the service is mid-restart, the finalize defers, and the rollup now shows… what? The plan stamps "the triggering predicate reason on every deferred/skipped record" and surfaces "a `finalize-deferred` count on the rollup" — a bare count. No named surface renders the REASON, the expected resolution ("retried automatically by the ~30-min sweep"), or the time-to-terminal. The user sees "3 deferred" for up to ~10 hours with no way to know whether that is self-healing or stuck — precisely the trained-to-ignore-the-banner hazard the locked healthcheck-severity rule exists to prevent. Worse, the healthcheck WARN threshold is unspecified ("when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals" — accumulate past WHAT?), so the one attention mechanism is undefined. And after `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` exhaustion the record silently becomes terminal `unmeasured` with the reason stamped on the record — again with no named surface showing the user that a session's spend was permanently given up and why. Specify: (a) the WARN threshold number, (b) which surface (session detail? rollup tooltip? `rnd spend`?) renders deferral reason + retry status + exhaustion outcome. Otherwise criterion 3's machinery is honest in the data layer and opaque at every surface the user actually reads.

findings.criterion: criteria 1 and 2 — swarm records must be visible on rendering surfaces
findings.message: The sweep mints child records with `session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`. On every surface that lists sessions (project window tiles, `rnd spend`, coverage report), that renders as an opaque UUID string with no label, no skill, no narration — a wall of `sidecar:a3f9…` rows for a 20-agent fleet. The walk-through specifies attribution mechanics thoroughly but never the display contract: are child rows rolled up under the parent's tile (recommended — "S + 5 sub-agents: 14.2M tok"), listed as first-class rows, or hidden behind an expander? A fleet-heavy project could show dozens of unlabeled synthetic rows, burying the real sessions — the exact clutter problem the v7 "most-recent prominent, older under an expander" pattern was built to avoid. Name the render rule in Phase 5.

findings.criterion: criterion 4 — the backfill's operational shape
findings.message: The backfill "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless `--force`." So the documented happy path for recovering history is: stop the Anchor service (dashboard goes dark), run a CLI, restart. Yet the plan's own trust-model row argues the tool is safe BY CONSTRUCTION regardless: exclusive-create claims cannot displace live records, terminal-status sessions only, snapshot-only reads. If the by-construction argument is sound, the service-down requirement is redundant ceremony that turns a one-command recovery into a service outage plus an elevated restart; if it is NOT sound, the trust-model row is overstated and `--force` (which re-enables the exact concurrent scenario) is under-guarded. Pick one: either drop the reachability refusal (keep the confirm flag) and let the CAS do its job, or state the concrete race the refusal prevents — "defense in depth" alone doesn't justify making the user take their own dashboard down, and in practice guarantees the recovery gets run with `--force` anyway, normalizing the override.

findings.criterion: criterion 3 — the hermetic predicate's closure claim
findings.message: The seam list is declared CLOSED: `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR`, `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`, `ANCHOR_WORKTREE_BASE`, `ANCHOR_SKILLS_DIR`, `ANCHOR_HEALTHCHECK`, `ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub`, `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD`, pytest-detection. But the healthcheck's own documented v4 walk also forces `ANCHOR_TERMINAL_SEED`, and the v8 test substrate forces `ANCHOR_GH_CMD` — both known hermetic markers absent from a list whose whole point is that closure is exhaustive. In practice any hermetic context also sets a listed seam, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a live hole — but a "CLOSED" list that misses known members on day one undermines the amendment discipline it's meant to establish (and the parametrized test will pass while the closure claim is already false). Sweep the codebase for every `ANCHOR_*` override at plan time and enumerate them all, or soften the closure claim to "the load-bearing subset."

findings.criterion: Statement ("honestly-provenanced… nothing is ever fabricated") — the plan's own provenance claims must meet the bar it sets for the product
findings.message: Changelog item 1 states, as completed fact: "The full second copy of the document embedded mid-item-2 of the launch-surface table is excised; the double phase numbering… is collapsed; the duplicated bulleted 'Success criteria' section is deleted; launch-table item 2 is restored intact… Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." Every one of these claims is false of the artifact it is attached to (see Finding 1 for the evidence). This is worse than the corruption itself: a plan whose entire theme is honest provenance ships a self-report that asserts fixes which demonstrably did not land. From the operator seat, this destroys the changelog's utility for the remaining rounds — John and the Judge can no longer take any "FIXED/STRENGTHENED/ADDED" claim on faith and must re-verify all six items by hand. The reviser's process (18 blind search/replace patches, per the revision log) produced no verification step that the patches applied to the intended locations; the re-emission must include a self-check (e.g., grep for `>>>>`, count North Star headers, count phase headers = 8) whose results are stated in the changelog as observed, not intended.

findings.criterion: Criterion 1 — swarm spend visible going forward requires an exhaustive, intact spawner enumeration
findings.message: The table is introduced as "tabled NOW — nothing left for Stage 2 to enumerate: every known spawner." Item 2 (`job_runner` one-shot lane jobs) still reads: "WIRED: envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)…" — truncated mid-parenthetical into an embedded copy of the entire document, with the orphaned fragment ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3); gains the pin so its sidecar correlates too." floating before item 3. The one row covering the entire one-shot job class (launch_lane, gate-driven runs, Gandalf's shard jobs route through job_runner) has no intact statement of its pinning mechanism or scope. A table that claims exhaustiveness while its second row is unreadable does not discharge criterion 1's enumeration burden; Stage 2 WOULD have something left to enumerate — exactly the thing the table says it doesn't.

findings.criterion: Criterion 1 — swarm launches pin `--session-id`
findings.message: The mechanism for the single most important population (106 of 111 registry sessions are swarm) is "the helper is exposed as a spawn-wrapper contract (an env-provided pin the dispatcher consumes at spawn)." An env-provided PIN is a single value; a 5:1 fleet dispatch spawns many sub-agents concurrently, each needing a UNIQUE session id minted and registered before exec. One env var cannot pin N spawns — either every sub-agent collides on the same pinned id (worse than today: N sidecars claiming one session), or the contract is actually "env-provided path to a wrapper executable that mints per-spawn," which is a materially different design the plan does not state. For the criterion the whole effort headlines, the plan hand-waves the exact interface at the exact fan-out point where it breaks. Specify the per-spawn minting protocol (wrapper binary? mint-endpoint the dispatcher calls per child? id-range lease?) or admit item 5 tier (a) is not designed yet and the sweep is the real mechanism.

findings.criterion: Criterion 1 — "A new fleet run produces measured records for its sub-agent sessions"
findings.section: Phase 3 item 5 / Phase 2 deferral / Phase 7 live receipt
findings.message: Phase 2 defers Gemini sidecar parsing — the fence "will refuse them honestly (`sidecar-format-unrecognized`)." But the 5:1 skill-layer swarm is by definition Gemini-majority: in a representative fleet run, five of every six sub-agent sessions will hit the fence and land `sidecar-format-unrecognized`, not `measured`. Phase 7's live proof — "trigger one small real fleet/swarm run and confirm sub-agent sessions produce measured records" — is therefore either unachievable for a representative fleet or will be satisfied by an unrepresentative all-Claude run (plausible right now because the cross-family seat is down, which quietly makes the receipt pass while the real 5:1 population stays unmeasured the day agy auth returns). The plan must state which outcome criterion 1 accepts: (a) criterion 1 is scoped to Claude sub-agents until the Gemini parser lands (then say so in the deferral AND the Phase 7 receipt), or (b) Gemini parsing is in scope after all. As written, the deferral and the live receipt contradict each other and the contradiction is invisible to the operator signing the receipt.

findings.criterion: Criterion 4 — history recovered
findings.message: Two operator-facing gaps around the same clock. First, Phase 0 says "execute NOW" but names no executor and no receipt-before-lock; the intake snapshot evidence is from 2026-07-18, the review loop is burning days, and every additional round is uninsured exposure to engine pruning of the only backfill asset. The lock should be conditioned on the Phase-0 manifest existing (an observed receipt), not on the plan text promising it. Second, Phase 3 asserts "after a long outage the first boot sweep catches up before engine pruning windows matter" — the engine's actual retention behavior (e.g., the CLI's cleanup period, whether it prunes by age or count) is nowhere observed or cited; this is exactly the kind of unverified assumption the plan elsewhere refuses to tolerate. Pin the observed retention setting in the intake evidence or downgrade the sentence to an honest unknown with the boot-sweep as best-effort.

findings.criterion: Criterion 6 — a session counts only if it contributed a measured record
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through mints child records (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) that have NO registry row by construction, while Phase 5's counting rule and the "N measured of M total" render are defined over registry sessions, and the synthetic predicate `is_synthetic_session(record)` keys off a registration flag child records never receive. Unspecified: do child rows increment N? M? Neither? Can a `__doctor__`-owned orchestrator spawn produce an un-flagged child row that leaks into a spend surface the synthetic predicate was supposed to fence? The two sections were written independently and don't compose; one sentence in Phase 5 defining child-row treatment (counted into effort totals, excluded from the session numerator/denominator, inherit the parent's synthetic flag) closes it.

findings.criterion: Criterion 3 — regression-tested hermetic behavior (mitigation 4's visibility leg)
findings.message: "Healthcheck WARN when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals" names no threshold or window. Per the locked severity rule the WARN is the operator's only tripwire for a silently-broken beacon; with no number it will either fire on the first routine deferral (trains the eye to ignore it — the exact hazard the severity rule exists to prevent) or be implemented as never-firing. Name the threshold (e.g., >K deferred records older than one sweep cadence).

findings.criterion: 1 commitment even if the cosmetic duplication were forgiven.)
findings.message: The table is introduced as "tabled NOW — nothing left for Stage 2 to enumerate," i.e. its exhaustiveness is load-bearing for criterion 1. But item 2 (`job_runner` one-shot lane jobs) is unrecoverable from this artifact in BOTH copies: each is cut mid-sentence by an embedded document. The closing fragment "…distinct per Stage-0 decision 3, plus the pin" hints at the intent (envelope-measured, real $, gains the pin), but a Stage-2 builder cannot reconstruct the wired mechanism for the second-largest launch surface from a hint. Either the table is complete in the emitted text or the "nothing left to enumerate" claim must be withdrawn. (Root cause is Finding 1; called out separately because it guts a specific

findings.criterion: 4 — "mints records with `usage_state: 'measured-backfill'`… reports an honest per-session outcome list" (and decision 2: "distinct provenance… auditable forever").
findings.section: Phase 3 (orphan sweep, unwrapped sub-agent walk-through) vs Phase 6 / Stage-0 decision 2
findings.message: Decision 2 defines `measured-backfill` as the distinct, forever-auditable provenance of the one-shot historical backfill against the frozen snapshot. Phase 3 then reuses the SAME value for two structurally different populations: forward orphan-sidecar sweep records and synthetic child rows (`sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) minted for unwrapped sub-agents — ongoing, indefinitely, from the LIVE sidecar root. Consequences: (a) the "auditable forever" property is destroyed — a future auditor cannot distinguish "recovered by the audited Phase-6 run from the snapshot" from "late-measured last Tuesday by the sweep"; (b) the plan's own single-owner matrix (backfill CLI owns pre-snapshot, sweep owns post-snapshot) becomes unverifiable from the records, because both owners write identical provenance; (c) reconciling the Phase-6 outcome list against the coverage report (a named Phase-6 task) is contaminated by sweep-minted rows carrying the same label. The closed `usage_state` vocabulary needs a distinct value (e.g. `measured-sweep`) for the forward path — and since the vocabulary is frozen in Phase 2 with a plan-amendment requirement, this must be decided NOW, not discovered at build time.

findings.criterion: 3 (hermetic skip) in tension with 1 and 2 (live sessions must actually get measured).
findings.message: The closed redirect-seam list includes "`ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` (stub runner)" — but the predicate has no way to know the parenthetical. `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` is ALSO a legitimate production wiring: `lanes.detect_host_profile` explicitly treats "a wired ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD" as Claude-available, i.e. a supported deploy configuration. If a live host (this one after a config change, or any distro host) wires the runner cmd legitimately, EVERY finalize — including the sweep's own retries, since the seam is process-wide env in the beaconed service — is forced to `finalize-deferred`, and the Phase-3 terminality rule then marches every record to terminal `unmeasured` after ~20 sweeps. Net effect: a supported configuration silently (yellow-WARN-only) zeroes the entire telemetry system — the exact "quietly returns to zeros" failure premortem #4 names. The plan must either (a) remove `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` from the seam list and rely on the other markers plus the hermetic-test conformance, or (b) define a testable discriminator between stub and legit wiring that is NOT name-sniffing (which the plan forbids elsewhere for good reason). As written, the seam list contains a known-legit production variable and no decision.

findings.criterion: 4 — the snapshot exists solely to preserve the worktree-dirname-correlated backfill asset.
findings.message: "Copy the ENTIRE engine sidecar root — every sidecar project dir, unfiltered" copies every Claude transcript on this machine — every personal, commercial, and unrelated-project conversation — into `.anchor/sidecar-archive/` inside the Anchor repo tree, and the justification ("the munging rule is untested, so we can't filter") is refuted BY THE SAME PHASE: the verification step performs "a read-only grep count" for the literal `…anchor-worktrees-<session_id>` marker, which is exactly the trivially-safe, non-munging filter that would bound the copy to the correlated population. The plan cannot simultaneously trust that grep to VERIFY the snapshot and distrust it to SCOPE the snapshot. Additionally, "the disk cost is bounded and recorded in the manifest" is not a bound — recording a size is not limiting it; a full `~/.claude/projects` root can be orders of magnitude larger than the 55+ target dirs, and the copy is proposed for immediate, unrepeatable execution. Refinement: copy dirs matching the literal worktree marker (over-inclusive on marker false-positives is fine), plus a listing-only manifest of everything NOT copied so nothing is silently unrecoverable if the marker grep later proves incomplete.

findings.criterion: 6 — "a session counts only if it contributed a measured record."
findings.section: Phase 3 walk-through vs Phase 5 honest counting
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent mechanism mints child records (`session_id: sidecar:<uuid>`) that are not registry sessions, and Phase 3 says "rollups sum child rows into the effort/fleet totals." Phase 5's honest-counting display is "N measured of M total" over registry sessions, and the Phase-5 coverage report is "the fraction of REGISTRY sessions." Unspecified: do child rows increment N (making N > M possible), appear in M, or appear only in token totals? Any of these is defensible, but the plan freezes the record schema and the counting rule in different phases without stating the interaction, so two builders will implement it two ways. One sentence in Phase 5 resolves it (recommend: child rows contribute tokens/$ but never to session counts; denominator stays registry-only).

findings.criterion: 5 — dollars are labeled estimates from a maintained table.
findings.message: "Assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" implies validation against a ground truth that the North Star's own non-goals guarantee cannot exist: the sidecar has no costUSD and provider billing integration is excluded. The only available comparand is a hand-computed expectation from the same pricing table — which makes the "error band" a disguised arithmetic-identity check, not an accuracy claim. Skeptical-researcher objection: shipping the phrase "declared error band" invites the reader to believe the estimates have been validated against real spend when they structurally cannot be. Rename the test to what it is (rate-arithmetic and category-selection correctness fixtures) and let the "est." label carry the honesty, per decision 3.

findings.criterion: 2 — "`__doctor__` is excluded from every surface."
findings.message: The predicate is driven by "an explicit `synthetic=True` REGISTRATION flag," and "`__doctor__` migrates onto the flag" — but the existing `__doctor__` sessions (visible in the live registry and this repo's git status) were registered without it. Who performs the one-off migration of existing records, in which phase, and is it audited like the other record mutations this plan is so careful about? Also unstated: whether the Phase-6 backfill target set excludes `__doctor__`/synthetic sessions from minting measured records at all, or mints them and relies on surface-level exclusion — the latter is consistent with criterion 2's letter but should be said out loud, since "excluded from every surface" and "absent from the record store" are different guarantees.

findings.criterion: 3 — the latch cannot be burned hermetically.
findings.message: The plan claims to "invert the hermetic predicate from blocklist to positive identity," but the actual predicate is (exclusive bind ∧ real data dir ∧ NO active seam from a closed list) — the third conjunct IS a blocklist, reintroduced because bind+data-dir alone would admit a future hermetic context that binds 8777 with the real data dir while the service is down. The three hermetic classes criterion 3 names (pytest, healthcheck, redirected data dir) are each covered by a listed marker, so the criterion is met — but the trust-model's row-1 honesty discipline ("residual, stated honestly") should be applied to the predicate itself: the residual is an UNLISTED future hermetic seam, bounded only by the plan-amendment convention. State it in the table rather than letting "no enumeration to get wrong" stand, which is true of supervisors but not of seams.

findings.criterion: 3 — "a later live finalize can still measure."
findings.message: "When its sidecar is absent from both the live root and the Phase-0 archive after `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` sweeps" is ambiguous between (a) absent at the 20th sweep and (b) absent for 20 CONSECUTIVE sweeps — under (a), a sidecar that existed for sweeps 1–19 (deferring for some other reason, e.g. quiesce or seam) and was then pruned by engine retention gets terminally `unmeasured` on its first absent observation, which is honest but harsher than the text implies; under (b) the counter must reset on any present-observation. Pick one and encode it in `test_deferred_terminality`, which currently pins only the exhaustion transition, not the counting rule.

findings.message: The changelog asserts, in past tense and as fact: "The full second copy … is excised; the double phase numbering … is collapsed; … launch-table item 2 is restored intact … Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." Every one of those statements is false of the emitted artifact (see Findings 1–2). For a plan whose entire theme is honest, verifiable claims ("never a fabricated 0", "vacuous-GREEN is a real failure mode here"), the plan document itself shipping a vacuous-GREEN changelog is disqualifying. The reviser's changelog to the Sharks was also 18 lines of "Applied a search/replace patch" with zero content — the review loop cannot converge when the revision record carries no information and the summary claims are unverified. Requirement: the next revision must be a from-scratch re-emission, and its changelog must be checkable against the artifact (e.g., "grep count of '# NORTH STAR' == 1").

findings.section: Phase 2 deferrals vs Phase 3 walk-through vs North Star Statement
findings.criterion: Statement ("Every Anchor surface that shows spend (project rollups, effort metrics, session details)") + criterion 6
findings.message: The Statement names three surfaces: project rollups, EFFORT METRICS, session details. Phase 2 explicitly defers "Per-effort fleet-attribution ROLLUP/QUERY itself — schema-ready now, query surface deferred to a future effort." Yet Phase 3's unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through promises the opposite: "rollups sum child rows into the effort/fleet totals with the backfill provenance visible." Which is it? Either child rows ARE summed into an effort total (then the per-effort query exists this effort and Phase 2's deferral is wrong), or the query is deferred (then Phase 3's promise is unbacked and swarm spend is NOT visible at the effort level — the exact surface a frustrated user looks at after a fleet run: "what did that effort cost me?"). As written, the user's most natural question has no named owner: Phase 5 delivers per-lane + general PROJECT lines only. The existing `effort_view.effort_rollup` surface (which shows per-effort Σtok·time·$ today) is also an enumerated rollup consumer that criterion 6's honest counting must touch — the plan greps for consumers in Phase 5 but never states whether effort tiles gain the measured/child-row numbers or keep showing zeros for swarm-heavy efforts. Resolve the contradiction explicitly and name which phase makes effort metrics true.

findings.criterion: criteria 2 and 3 — surfaces must render honestly-provenanced states, and the deferral machinery is user-visible
findings.message: The frustrated-UX walk: a user closes a session while the service is mid-restart, the finalize defers, and the rollup now shows… what? The plan stamps "the triggering predicate reason on every deferred/skipped record" and surfaces "a `finalize-deferred` count on the rollup" — a bare count. No named surface renders the REASON, the expected resolution ("retried automatically by the ~30-min sweep"), or the time-to-terminal. The user sees "3 deferred" for up to ~10 hours with no way to know whether that is self-healing or stuck — precisely the trained-to-ignore-the-banner hazard the locked healthcheck-severity rule exists to prevent. Worse, the healthcheck WARN threshold is unspecified ("when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals" — accumulate past WHAT?), so the one attention mechanism is undefined. And after `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` exhaustion the record silently becomes terminal `unmeasured` with the reason stamped on the record — again with no named surface showing the user that a session's spend was permanently given up and why. Specify: (a) the WARN threshold number, (b) which surface (session detail? rollup tooltip? `rnd spend`?) renders deferral reason + retry status + exhaustion outcome. Otherwise criterion 3's machinery is honest in the data layer and opaque at every surface the user actually reads.

findings.criterion: criteria 1 and 2 — swarm records must be visible on rendering surfaces
findings.message: The sweep mints child records with `session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`. On every surface that lists sessions (project window tiles, `rnd spend`, coverage report), that renders as an opaque UUID string with no label, no skill, no narration — a wall of `sidecar:a3f9…` rows for a 20-agent fleet. The walk-through specifies attribution mechanics thoroughly but never the display contract: are child rows rolled up under the parent's tile (recommended — "S + 5 sub-agents: 14.2M tok"), listed as first-class rows, or hidden behind an expander? A fleet-heavy project could show dozens of unlabeled synthetic rows, burying the real sessions — the exact clutter problem the v7 "most-recent prominent, older under an expander" pattern was built to avoid. Name the render rule in Phase 5.

findings.criterion: criterion 4 — the backfill's operational shape
findings.message: The backfill "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless `--force`." So the documented happy path for recovering history is: stop the Anchor service (dashboard goes dark), run a CLI, restart. Yet the plan's own trust-model row argues the tool is safe BY CONSTRUCTION regardless: exclusive-create claims cannot displace live records, terminal-status sessions only, snapshot-only reads. If the by-construction argument is sound, the service-down requirement is redundant ceremony that turns a one-command recovery into a service outage plus an elevated restart; if it is NOT sound, the trust-model row is overstated and `--force` (which re-enables the exact concurrent scenario) is under-guarded. Pick one: either drop the reachability refusal (keep the confirm flag) and let the CAS do its job, or state the concrete race the refusal prevents — "defense in depth" alone doesn't justify making the user take their own dashboard down, and in practice guarantees the recovery gets run with `--force` anyway, normalizing the override.

findings.criterion: criterion 3 — the hermetic predicate's closure claim
findings.message: The seam list is declared CLOSED: `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR`, `ANCHOR_SIDECAR_DIR`, `ANCHOR_WORKTREE_BASE`, `ANCHOR_SKILLS_DIR`, `ANCHOR_HEALTHCHECK`, `ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub`, `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD`, pytest-detection. But the healthcheck's own documented v4 walk also forces `ANCHOR_TERMINAL_SEED`, and the v8 test substrate forces `ANCHOR_GH_CMD` — both known hermetic markers absent from a list whose whole point is that closure is exhaustive. In practice any hermetic context also sets a listed seam, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a live hole — but a "CLOSED" list that misses known members on day one undermines the amendment discipline it's meant to establish (and the parametrized test will pass while the closure claim is already false). Sweep the codebase for every `ANCHOR_*` override at plan time and enumerate them all, or soften the closure claim to "the load-bearing subset."

reviews.note: Reviewed as Contrarian Shark, pressing the operator angle. The dominant fact about this "clean re-emission" is that it is not clean — the corruption the Synthesizer held the lock on is still present, and the changelog claims otherwise. I verified each claim against the emitted text before writing these findings.

findings.criterion: all six criteria — every phase-to-criterion mapping depends on a single unambiguous document
findings.message: The Round-3 mechanical note promises "ONE North Star copy, ONE copy of each phase, single phase numbering 0–7." The emitted artifact delivers none of that. Concretely observable in the text: (a) raw search/replace patch markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) appear literally after the intake-evidence section, followed by BOTH the new "Eight phases, numbered 0–7" overview AND the old "Seven phases" paragraph it was supposed to replace — the document now asserts two different phase counts in adjacent paragraphs; (b) the old double-numbered headers ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 2 — Phase 1 —", …, "Phase 4 — Phase 3 —" immediately followed by a second "Phase 4 — Pricing engine") are still present inside an entire embedded second copy of the document; (c) that embedded copy itself embeds a THIRD copy (the "Round-3 re-emission" header recurs inside the changelog), i.e. the North Star appears at least three times; (d) the duplicated bulleted "Success criteria" section the changelog claims was deleted is still present twice. An operator or a Stage-2 Foreman consuming this document cannot resolve "Phase 6" or "Phase 4" to a unique section. This is the same not-lockable cause Round 2 identified, unresolved. The fix is purely mechanical — emit the document once, from scratch, not via search/replace patches over a corrupted base — but until it happens nothing else in this review can lock.

findings.criterion: Statement ("honestly-provenanced… nothing is ever fabricated") — the plan's own provenance claims must meet the bar it sets for the product
findings.message: Changelog item 1 states, as completed fact: "The full second copy of the document embedded mid-item-2 of the launch-surface table is excised; the double phase numbering… is collapsed; the duplicated bulleted 'Success criteria' section is deleted; launch-table item 2 is restored intact… Exactly ONE North Star copy remains." Every one of these claims is false of the artifact it is attached to (see Finding 1 for the evidence). This is worse than the corruption itself: a plan whose entire theme is honest provenance ships a self-report that asserts fixes which demonstrably did not land. From the operator seat, this destroys the changelog's utility for the remaining rounds — John and the Judge can no longer take any "FIXED/STRENGTHENED/ADDED" claim on faith and must re-verify all six items by hand. The reviser's process (18 blind search/replace patches, per the revision log) produced no verification step that the patches applied to the intended locations; the re-emission must include a self-check (e.g., grep for `>>>>`, count North Star headers, count phase headers = 8) whose results are stated in the changelog as observed, not intended.

findings.criterion: Criterion 1 — swarm spend visible going forward requires an exhaustive, intact spawner enumeration
findings.message: The table is introduced as "tabled NOW — nothing left for Stage 2 to enumerate: every known spawner." Item 2 (`job_runner` one-shot lane jobs) still reads: "WIRED: envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)…" — truncated mid-parenthetical into an embedded copy of the entire document, with the orphaned fragment ", stays distinct per Stage-0 decision 3); gains the pin so its sidecar correlates too." floating before item 3. The one row covering the entire one-shot job class (launch_lane, gate-driven runs, Gandalf's shard jobs route through job_runner) has no intact statement of its pinning mechanism or scope. A table that claims exhaustiveness while its second row is unreadable does not discharge criterion 1's enumeration burden; Stage 2 WOULD have something left to enumerate — exactly the thing the table says it doesn't.

findings.criterion: Criterion 1 — swarm launches pin `--session-id`
findings.message: The mechanism for the single most important population (106 of 111 registry sessions are swarm) is "the helper is exposed as a spawn-wrapper contract (an env-provided pin the dispatcher consumes at spawn)." An env-provided PIN is a single value; a 5:1 fleet dispatch spawns many sub-agents concurrently, each needing a UNIQUE session id minted and registered before exec. One env var cannot pin N spawns — either every sub-agent collides on the same pinned id (worse than today: N sidecars claiming one session), or the contract is actually "env-provided path to a wrapper executable that mints per-spawn," which is a materially different design the plan does not state. For the criterion the whole effort headlines, the plan hand-waves the exact interface at the exact fan-out point where it breaks. Specify the per-spawn minting protocol (wrapper binary? mint-endpoint the dispatcher calls per child? id-range lease?) or admit item 5 tier (a) is not designed yet and the sweep is the real mechanism.

findings.section: Phase 3 item 5 / Phase 2 deferral / Phase 7 live receipt
findings.criterion: Criterion 1 — "A new fleet run produces measured records for its sub-agent sessions"
findings.message: Phase 2 defers Gemini sidecar parsing — the fence "will refuse them honestly (`sidecar-format-unrecognized`)." But the 5:1 skill-layer swarm is by definition Gemini-majority: in a representative fleet run, five of every six sub-agent sessions will hit the fence and land `sidecar-format-unrecognized`, not `measured`. Phase 7's live proof — "trigger one small real fleet/swarm run and confirm sub-agent sessions produce measured records" — is therefore either unachievable for a representative fleet or will be satisfied by an unrepresentative all-Claude run (plausible right now because the cross-family seat is down, which quietly makes the receipt pass while the real 5:1 population stays unmeasured the day agy auth returns). The plan must state which outcome criterion 1 accepts: (a) criterion 1 is scoped to Claude sub-agents until the Gemini parser lands (then say so in the deferral AND the Phase 7 receipt), or (b) Gemini parsing is in scope after all. As written, the deferral and the live receipt contradict each other and the contradiction is invisible to the operator signing the receipt.

findings.criterion: Criterion 4 — history recovered
findings.message: Two operator-facing gaps around the same clock. First, Phase 0 says "execute NOW" but names no executor and no receipt-before-lock; the intake snapshot evidence is from 2026-07-18, the review loop is burning days, and every additional round is uninsured exposure to engine pruning of the only backfill asset. The lock should be conditioned on the Phase-0 manifest existing (an observed receipt), not on the plan text promising it. Second, Phase 3 asserts "after a long outage the first boot sweep catches up before engine pruning windows matter" — the engine's actual retention behavior (e.g., the CLI's cleanup period, whether it prunes by age or count) is nowhere observed or cited; this is exactly the kind of unverified assumption the plan elsewhere refuses to tolerate. Pin the observed retention setting in the intake evidence or downgrade the sentence to an honest unknown with the boot-sweep as best-effort.

findings.topic: child sidecar records vs counting semantics
findings.criterion: Criterion 6 — a session counts only if it contributed a measured record
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent walk-through mints child records (`session_id: sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) that have NO registry row by construction, while Phase 5's counting rule and the "N measured of M total" render are defined over registry sessions, and the synthetic predicate `is_synthetic_session(record)` keys off a registration flag child records never receive. Unspecified: do child rows increment N? M? Neither? Can a `__doctor__`-owned orchestrator spawn produce an un-flagged child row that leaks into a spend surface the synthetic predicate was supposed to fence? The two sections were written independently and don't compose; one sentence in Phase 5 defining child-row treatment (counted into effort totals, excluded from the session numerator/denominator, inherit the parent's synthetic flag) closes it.

findings.criterion: Criterion 3 — regression-tested hermetic behavior (mitigation 4's visibility leg)
findings.message: "Healthcheck WARN when live-registry sessions accumulate deferrals" names no threshold or window. Per the locked severity rule the WARN is the operator's only tripwire for a silently-broken beacon; with no number it will either fire on the first routine deferral (trains the eye to ignore it — the exact hazard the severity rule exists to prevent) or be implemented as never-firing. Name the threshold (e.g., >K deferred records older than one sweep cadence).

reviews.note: This "Round-3 re-emission, deduplicated" is judged as the emitted artifact, not as its changelog describes itself. The artifact observably fails the mechanical requirement it opens by claiming to satisfy.

findings.criterion: All six — a plan whose phase references cannot be resolved serves none of them; most acutely criterion 4 ("Phase 6 backfill" / "Phase-0 snapshot" cross-references) and criterion 1 (the launch-surface table).
findings.message: The re-emission FAILED its own stated requirement and the corruption the Synthesizer ruled not-lockable is still present, in every form the changelog claims was fixed. Observable in this artifact: (a) raw search/replace diff markers (`>>>>`, `<<<<`, `====`) appear verbatim in the body — twice; (b) at least THREE full North Star copies are embedded (the header copy, one inside the first embedded "Master Plan (draft)", one inside the second embedded copy that interrupts the changelog), while the closing line asserts "Exactly ONE North Star copy remains" — the document makes a claim that is false of itself; (c) the double phase numbering survives ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 —", "Phase 2 — Phase 1 —", "Phase 3 — Phase 2 —", "Phase 4 — Phase 3 —") alongside the single-numbered scheme, including TWO distinct sections titled "Phase 4"; (d) launch-surface table item 2 is again severed mid-parenthesis by an embedded full document copy ("envelope-measured today (real `# Master Plan (draft)…`") — the very item the round-3 note claims was "restored intact"; (e) changelog item 1 is itself interrupted by the second full-document embedding, and the reviser's changelog ("Applied a search/replace patch" ×18) shows patches were applied into the corrupted artifact with no post-emission verification read. A builder cannot determine which of the duplicated, mutually-inconsistent phase texts is authoritative (the duplicated Phase-1 copies differ substantively: one has the beacon consume-time re-verification and writer row 6, the other does not). This is not lockable. The fix is not another patch series — it is a genuinely clean single re-emission, followed by an actual read-back of the emitted file before submission.

findings.criterion: 1 commitment even if the cosmetic duplication were forgiven.)
findings.message: The table is introduced as "tabled NOW — nothing left for Stage 2 to enumerate," i.e. its exhaustiveness is load-bearing for criterion 1. But item 2 (`job_runner` one-shot lane jobs) is unrecoverable from this artifact in BOTH copies: each is cut mid-sentence by an embedded document. The closing fragment "…distinct per Stage-0 decision 3, plus the pin" hints at the intent (envelope-measured, real $, gains the pin), but a Stage-2 builder cannot reconstruct the wired mechanism for the second-largest launch surface from a hint. Either the table is complete in the emitted text or the "nothing left to enumerate" claim must be withdrawn. (Root cause is Finding 1; called out separately because it guts a specific

findings.section: Phase 3 (orphan sweep, unwrapped sub-agent walk-through) vs Phase 6 / Stage-0 decision 2
findings.criterion: 4 — "mints records with `usage_state: 'measured-backfill'`… reports an honest per-session outcome list" (and decision 2: "distinct provenance… auditable forever").
findings.message: Decision 2 defines `measured-backfill` as the distinct, forever-auditable provenance of the one-shot historical backfill against the frozen snapshot. Phase 3 then reuses the SAME value for two structurally different populations: forward orphan-sidecar sweep records and synthetic child rows (`sidecar:<engine-uuid>`) minted for unwrapped sub-agents — ongoing, indefinitely, from the LIVE sidecar root. Consequences: (a) the "auditable forever" property is destroyed — a future auditor cannot distinguish "recovered by the audited Phase-6 run from the snapshot" from "late-measured last Tuesday by the sweep"; (b) the plan's own single-owner matrix (backfill CLI owns pre-snapshot, sweep owns post-snapshot) becomes unverifiable from the records, because both owners write identical provenance; (c) reconciling the Phase-6 outcome list against the coverage report (a named Phase-6 task) is contaminated by sweep-minted rows carrying the same label. The closed `usage_state` vocabulary needs a distinct value (e.g. `measured-sweep`) for the forward path — and since the vocabulary is frozen in Phase 2 with a plan-amendment requirement, this must be decided NOW, not discovered at build time.

findings.criterion: 3 (hermetic skip) in tension with 1 and 2 (live sessions must actually get measured).
findings.message: The closed redirect-seam list includes "`ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` (stub runner)" — but the predicate has no way to know the parenthetical. `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` is ALSO a legitimate production wiring: `lanes.detect_host_profile` explicitly treats "a wired ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD" as Claude-available, i.e. a supported deploy configuration. If a live host (this one after a config change, or any distro host) wires the runner cmd legitimately, EVERY finalize — including the sweep's own retries, since the seam is process-wide env in the beaconed service — is forced to `finalize-deferred`, and the Phase-3 terminality rule then marches every record to terminal `unmeasured` after ~20 sweeps. Net effect: a supported configuration silently (yellow-WARN-only) zeroes the entire telemetry system — the exact "quietly returns to zeros" failure premortem #4 names. The plan must either (a) remove `ANCHOR_RUNNER_CMD` from the seam list and rely on the other markers plus the hermetic-test conformance, or (b) define a testable discriminator between stub and legit wiring that is NOT name-sniffing (which the plan forbids elsewhere for good reason). As written, the seam list contains a known-legit production variable and no decision.

findings.criterion: 4 — the snapshot exists solely to preserve the worktree-dirname-correlated backfill asset.
findings.message: "Copy the ENTIRE engine sidecar root — every sidecar project dir, unfiltered" copies every Claude transcript on this machine — every personal, commercial, and unrelated-project conversation — into `.anchor/sidecar-archive/` inside the Anchor repo tree, and the justification ("the munging rule is untested, so we can't filter") is refuted BY THE SAME PHASE: the verification step performs "a read-only grep count" for the literal `…anchor-worktrees-<session_id>` marker, which is exactly the trivially-safe, non-munging filter that would bound the copy to the correlated population. The plan cannot simultaneously trust that grep to VERIFY the snapshot and distrust it to SCOPE the snapshot. Additionally, "the disk cost is bounded and recorded in the manifest" is not a bound — recording a size is not limiting it; a full `~/.claude/projects` root can be orders of magnitude larger than the 55+ target dirs, and the copy is proposed for immediate, unrepeatable execution. Refinement: copy dirs matching the literal worktree marker (over-inclusive on marker false-positives is fine), plus a listing-only manifest of everything NOT copied so nothing is silently unrecoverable if the marker grep later proves incomplete.

findings.section: Phase 3 walk-through vs Phase 5 honest counting
findings.criterion: 6 — "a session counts only if it contributed a measured record."
findings.message: The unwrapped-sub-agent mechanism mints child records (`session_id: sidecar:<uuid>`) that are not registry sessions, and Phase 3 says "rollups sum child rows into the effort/fleet totals." Phase 5's honest-counting display is "N measured of M total" over registry sessions, and the Phase-5 coverage report is "the fraction of REGISTRY sessions." Unspecified: do child rows increment N (making N > M possible), appear in M, or appear only in token totals? Any of these is defensible, but the plan freezes the record schema and the counting rule in different phases without stating the interaction, so two builders will implement it two ways. One sentence in Phase 5 resolves it (recommend: child rows contribute tokens/$ but never to session counts; denominator stays registry-only).

findings.criterion: 5 — dollars are labeled estimates from a maintained table.
findings.message: "Assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" implies validation against a ground truth that the North Star's own non-goals guarantee cannot exist: the sidecar has no costUSD and provider billing integration is excluded. The only available comparand is a hand-computed expectation from the same pricing table — which makes the "error band" a disguised arithmetic-identity check, not an accuracy claim. Skeptical-researcher objection: shipping the phrase "declared error band" invites the reader to believe the estimates have been validated against real spend when they structurally cannot be. Rename the test to what it is (rate-arithmetic and category-selection correctness fixtures) and let the "est." label carry the honesty, per decision 3.

findings.criterion: 2 — "`__doctor__` is excluded from every surface."
findings.message: The predicate is driven by "an explicit `synthetic=True` REGISTRATION flag," and "`__doctor__` migrates onto the flag" — but the existing `__doctor__` sessions (visible in the live registry and this repo's git status) were registered without it. Who performs the one-off migration of existing records, in which phase, and is it audited like the other record mutations this plan is so careful about? Also unstated: whether the Phase-6 backfill target set excludes `__doctor__`/synthetic sessions from minting measured records at all, or mints them and relies on surface-level exclusion — the latter is consistent with criterion 2's letter but should be said out loud, since "excluded from every surface" and "absent from the record store" are different guarantees.

findings.criterion: 3 — the latch cannot be burned hermetically.
findings.message: The plan claims to "invert the hermetic predicate from blocklist to positive identity," but the actual predicate is (exclusive bind ∧ real data dir ∧ NO active seam from a closed list) — the third conjunct IS a blocklist, reintroduced because bind+data-dir alone would admit a future hermetic context that binds 8777 with the real data dir while the service is down. The three hermetic classes criterion 3 names (pytest, healthcheck, redirected data dir) are each covered by a listed marker, so the criterion is met — but the trust-model's row-1 honesty discipline ("residual, stated honestly") should be applied to the predicate itself: the residual is an UNLISTED future hermetic seam, bounded only by the plan-amendment convention. State it in the table rather than letting "no enumeration to get wrong" stand, which is true of supervisors but not of seams.

findings.criterion: 3 — "a later live finalize can still measure."
findings.message: "When its sidecar is absent from both the live root and the Phase-0 archive after `DEFER_RETRY_MAX` sweeps" is ambiguous between (a) absent at the 20th sweep and (b) absent for 20 CONSECUTIVE sweeps — under (a), a sidecar that existed for sweeps 1–19 (deferring for some other reason, e.g. quiesce or seam) and was then pruned by engine retention gets terminally `unmeasured` on its first absent observation, which is honest but harsher than the text implies; under (b) the counter must reset on any present-observation. Pick one and encode it in `test_deferred_terminality`, which currently pins only the exhaustion transition, not the counting rule.
